name_native: 日月潭阿薩姆紅茶（台茶8號）
processing: Fully oxidised orthodox black from large Assam-type leaf: withered, rolled into thick twisted strips, oxidised and dried; no roast. Most is hand-picked bud-and-two-leaves and sold loose; some goes to teabags and drink shops.
harvest_season: Summer leaf (June–August) is the strongest and most typical; spring and autumn lots are softer.
appearance_dry: Large, thick, dark twisted strips, chunkier and less wiry than Ruby 18.
taste_profile: Bold, malty and dark-honeyed with a cocoa edge and a firm, brisk body that stands up to milk; less perfumed than Ruby 18 and closer to an Indian Assam.

brewing.notes: Western-style, 3 g per 250 ml at 90–95 °C for three minutes, is how most people drink it; brewed hard it turns tannic like an Indian Assam. Takes milk and sugar well and cold-brews smoothly.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year and season, with summer leaf the most typical, at a fraction of the price of Ruby 18, which is why much tea labelled only 'Sun Moon Lake black tea' is TTES #8; ask for the cultivar if it matters. It is graded in the Yuchi Farmers' Association competition alongside the newer cultivars and carries the area's certified-origin label. Keeps two or three years sealed.
description:
Sun Moon Lake Assam is the black tea that Yuchi Township in Nantou was built on: an Assam-type bush grown around the lake since the Japanese period and known as cultivar number 8. Plantations of Indian tea varieties were developed in Yuchi in the 1920s, and the Yuchi Black Tea Research Institute was founded in 1926.

The cultivar is a large-leaf Assam in character, so the tea is the opposite of the island's delicate small-leaf blacks: thick, dark twisted strips, a deep red-brown liquor and a bold, malty, cocoa-edged cup with real briskness. It is made orthodox-style, withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried, with no roast; most of it is hand-picked bud-and-two-leaves and sold loose, though some goes into teabags and drink-shop supply.

In the cup, expect malt, dark honey, a cocoa bitterness and a firm body that stands up to milk and sugar better than any other Taiwanese tea; it is the natural base for Taiwanese milk tea. Brewed gently, 90 to 95 degrees and three minutes, it is smooth enough to drink neat; brewed hard it turns tannic in the way an Indian Assam does. It cold-brews well and the chill rounds the edges.

It is sold by harvest year and season, with summer leaf the strongest and most typical, and it costs much less than Ruby 18, which is why a lot of tea labelled just 'Sun Moon Lake black tea' is actually number 8; ask for the cultivar if it matters to you. The Yuchi Farmers' Association grades it in its competition alongside the newer cultivars, and the area's certified-origin label applies. It keeps for two or three years sealed.

Taste it next to Ruby 18 to see what the breeders added when they crossed Assam with Taiwan's wild tea: the body is the same, the mint and cinnamon are new.
history: This is the Assam-type black tea of Yuchi Township, by Sun Moon Lake in Nantou. Plantations of Indian tea varieties were developed in Yuchi in the 1920s, and the Yuchi Black Tea Research Institute was founded in 1926. Today the name Sun Moon Lake black tea is attached mainly to the newer Hongyu, or Ruby 18, so this older cultivar, number 8, is easily confused with it. The date of its release as a named cultivar is not confirmed here.
